name: SKYGEN
desc:
Customer Care Rep II | $16.42 to $24.63/hr plus $2/hr Mon and Tue | Inbound Dental and Vision Calls, No Sales Expectations
Company: SKYGEN
Industry: Insurance Services

What Your Day Will Look Like:
SKYGEN runs dental and vision benefits for insurance plans and government agencies. In this role, you take inbound calls from members and from dental and vision providers. You'll answer questions about eligibility, coverage, authorizations, and claims, and help members find a provider near them. For providers, you'll use what you know about claim adjustments and resubmissions to find the right fix, check on credentialing applications, and show them how to use the provider web portal. You'll also help with enrollment, like assigning primary care providers and updating other insurance, and work with the client's member services team on appeals and grievances. Every call gets documented in the system. Training is 12 weeks, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central.

Soft Skills
- Empathy and patience
- Active listening
- Problem solving and critical thinking
- Calming upset callers
- Attention to detail
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent
Required Experience: 1+ years of customer service in healthcare, call center, banking, or retail
Preferred Experience: 1+ years of customer service in dental, vision, or medical. Remote work experience. Knowledge of dental, vision, or medical insurance terms.

Required Skills:
- Basic Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook)
- Excellent listening and communication
- Strong customer service and empathy
- Strong data entry and typing
- Navigating multiple systems and multitasking
- Excellent attention to detail
- Critical thinking to find the right answer quickly
- Able to work occasional overtime

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has a year of call center, retail, banking, or healthcare customer service
- Has worked at a dentist or doctor's office or with insurance claims
- Wants an early weekday start with most evenings and weekends off
- Likes solving problems and learning insurance details

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Has less than 1 year of customer service experience
- Doesn't want to be on the phone most of the day
- Can't commit to 12 weeks of daytime training
- Can't work some evenings or weekends during Medicare open enrollment
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Inbound call center
- Dental and vision benefits
- Eligibility verification
- Claims and authorizations
- Provider support
- Enrollment support
- Appeals and grievances
- Call documentation
- Insurance terminology
- Customer service

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your customer service experience and the kinds of calls you've handled.
- A member wants to know if a dental cleaning is covered. How would you help them?
- How would you handle a provider who is frustrated that a claim hasn't been paid?
- Tell us about a time you calmed an upset customer and solved their problem. What was the situation, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you had to learn a lot of new information quickly. What did you need to learn, how did you do it, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $16.42 to $24.63/hr, plus a $2.00/hr differential on Mondays and Tuesdays.
-Shift: Training is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central for the first 12 weeks. After training, start times range from 6:00 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. Central, Monday through Friday. Hours of operation are 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. Central, so shifts can flex. Occasional evenings, weekends, and holidays may be needed during Medicare open enrollment (October 1 to March 31).
-Benefits: Basic benefits: insurance options, PTO, possible 401k
-Equipment Provided: Yes
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case
-Drug Test: Certain positions
-Notes: This is a weekday daytime job after training, plus a pay bump on Mondays and Tuesdays. Healthcare or insurance experience helps but isn't required beyond 1 year of customer service. Medicare open enrollment runs October through March, so anyone hired now should expect some extra hours early on. Camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Customer Care Rep II → Senior Customer Care Rep → Portal Services or Provider Relations Rep → Team Lead → Customer Care Supervisor. This role builds insurance claims, eligibility, and provider support skills.
training: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. M-F Central, first 12 weeks
